title: Prediction of Deep Neural Network for TCAD Analysis of Degradation Induced by Near-Interface Displacement Defects in 4H-SiC MOSFETs
content: Silicon carbide (SiC) devices used in space and nuclear environments are exposed to radiation that creates displacement defects, and the effect of these defects near the gate oxide/SiC interface has not been analyzed systematically. This paper analyzes the effects of displacement defects (DDs) near this interface in a 4H-SiC metal-oxide-semiconductor field-effect transistor (MOSFET) on the threshold voltage (Vth), transconductance (gm), and on-current (Ion) using technology computer-aided design (TCAD) simulation, and builds deep neural network (DNN) models that predict these effects. The DDs were modeled as acceptor-like traps, and their energy level, concentration, depth, lateral position, and distribution width were varied. The degradation was largest when the traps were located in the channel and at the edge of the junction field-effect transistor (JFET) region, and the depth mattered little as long as the trap region reached the interface. In addition, shallow-level traps reduced Ion without shifting Vth, whereas deep-level traps also increased Vth. All three DNN models for Vth, gm, and Ion reproduced the TCAD simulation results with high accuracy. Because the trained DNNs can rapidly predict the degradation for trap conditions not used in training within the valid range, they can be used for radiation reliability assessment of SiC MOSFETs.
